title: Routing Rule Contract Refinery: DSL→IR schema validation and staged rollout
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Background: Our routing policy DSL has accumulated special-case knobs for region affinity, tier routing, and fallback model variants. That has made validation brittle and produced subtle production rollouts where incompatible configs slip through.

Goal: Replace the current ad-hoc validators with a focused "contract refinery" step that canonicalizes DSL rules into a small typed IR and validates a strict schema plus richer semantic constraints (region/tier cross-checks, variant compatibility matrices, and fallback transitive closure). Deliver a migration path that allows old configs to be auto-canonicalized where possible and surfaces clear upgrade guidance where not.

Scope:
- Implement DSL->IR canonicalizer that normalizes synonyms (region_aliases, tier aliases, legacy variant names).
- Add a modular schema validation pipeline: syntactic checks -> typed AST checks -> semantic rules (region availability, hardware-capability constraints, tier preemption rules) -> compatibility check for fallback variants.
- Backcompat shim that emits transformation suggestions and a per-config "migration score".
- CLI and API validation endpoints for pings in CI and preflight checks in Console.
- Integration tests and a lightweight simulator to exercise fallback resolution across region outages.

Out-of-scope: full policy interpreter rewrite; runtime routing runtime changes (only the validator/canonicalizer + migration plan).

Acceptance criteria:
- New validator rejects 95%+ of malformed configs that previously passed (measured on historical config corpus).
- Auto-canonicalization successfully rewrites >= 80% of historical configs without semantic drift (validated by summerization tests).
- Rollout plan exists with feature flag gating and canary on 5% of accounts.
- Console preflight shows clear migration actions and links to generated transformation PRs.
- Unit + integration test coverage >= 85% for new modules.

Design notes & trade-offs:
- We chose a small typed IR (explicit enums for region, tier, variant families) to make downstream checks deterministic — tradeoff is extra migration surface.
- Validation pipeline is staged to allow fast syntactic failures to return quickly for CI, while deeper semantic checks run asynchronously for large customers.
- We will not attempt to reconcile historical variants with different semantics automatically; instead we will flag these with a "manual review recommended" score.

Migration strategy:
1) Run canonicalizer in dry-run mode against the config corpus and produce per-config diffs.
2) For configs with trivial rewrites, auto-apply behind a migration FF and record telemetry.
3) For flagged configs, surface a migration PR template + admin console action item.
4) Monitor preflight errors and SLO regressions for 2 weeks before wide rollout.

Testing plan:
- Unit tests for canonicalizer (aliases, edge-cases), typed AST validations, and semantic rule engine.
- Property tests using fuzzed routing rules (ensure invariants: fallback reachability, region-tier consistency).
- Integration test harness that simulates region failure and validates fallback variant selection.
- Backcompat tests: run historical corpus through dry-run and compare semantics with baseline interpreter.

Rollout plan:
- Ship behind feature flag policy_refinery_v1.
- Canary on internal accounts + 5 pilot customers (opt-in).
- After 2 weeks of canary and resolving issues, expand to 25% then 100% with telemetry checks at each step.

Observability & safety:
- Add telemetry for validator rejects, auto-canonicalizations, migration_score buckets, and semantic error categories.
- Add SLO guardrails: if canonicalizer-caused routing mismatches exceed threshold (0.1% of requests with significant path delta), auto-disable auto-apply and notify on-call.

Deliverables:
- RFC + design doc (links in attachments).
- Canonicalizer library and validator microservice with REST/CLI hooks.
- Console preflight UI bits (PM + design scope).
- Migration tooling that generates diffs and PR templates.

Open questions:
- What is the final shape of the variant compatibility matrix? (Need input from model-ops on model interchangeability semantics.)
- Should we incorporate hardware capability validation now or defer until runtime routing SR?

Estimated effort: 13pts across 6 sprints (engineering + QA + SRE for rollout).
